leaving the suspension into an electrical path.”

11.1 Mechanical State
Consider a translational mechanical coordinate
x(t),
with velocity
v(t)=\dot x(t)
and acceleration
a(t)=\ddot x(t).
For a body of mass m>0, kinetic energy is
T
=
\frac12m\dot x^2.
If the body is connected to a linear spring of stiffness k>0,
elastic potential energy is
U
=
\frac12kx^2.
The total stored mechanical energy is

 E_m
=
\frac12m\dot x^2
+
\frac12kx^2.

11.2 Mechanical Work and Power
For force F, infinitesimal work is
dW=F\,dx.
Instantaneous mechanical power is
P_m
=
F\dot x.

Proposition 11.1 — Sign of mechanical power
• If
F\dot x>0,
the force supplies energy to the coordinate.
• If
F\dot x<0,
the force extracts energy from the coordinate.
• If
F\dot x=0,
the force transfers no instantaneous power.

Proof

 Power is the time derivative of work:
P_m
=
\frac{dW}{dt}
=
F\frac{dx}{dt}
=
F\dot x.
Its sign determines the direction of energy transfer. ∎

11.3 Linear Spring–Mass–Damper
Consider
m\ddot x+c\dot x+kx=F_{\mathrm{ext}}(t),
with damping coefficient c\ge0.
Multiply by \dot x:
m\ddot x\dot x
+
c\dot x^2
+
kx\dot x
=
F_{\mathrm{ext}}\dot x.
Recognize

 m\ddot x\dot x
=
\frac{d}{dt}
\left(
\frac12m\dot x^2
\right),
and
kx\dot x
=
\frac{d}{dt}
\left(
\frac12kx^2
\right).
Therefore
\frac{dE_m}{dt}
+
c\dot x^2
=
F_{\mathrm{ext}}\dot x.

Theorem 11.2 — Mechanical energy balance
For the linear spring–mass–damper system,
\boxed{
\frac{dE_m}{dt}
=

 P_{\mathrm{ext}}
P_{\mathrm{diss}}
}
where
P_{\mathrm{ext}}
=
F_{\mathrm{ext}}\dot x
and
P_{\mathrm{diss}}
=
c\dot x^2\ge0.

Proof
The identity follows from the calculation above. ∎
The damper removes mechanical energy at a nonnegative
rate.

11.4 Passive Viscous Damping
The viscous damper force is
F_d=-c\dot x.
Its mechanical power on the moving mass is

 P_d
=
F_d\dot x
=
-c\dot x^2
\le0.
Thus an ideal viscous damper never injects energy into the
mechanical coordinate.

Definition 11.1 — Passive mechanical element
An element is passive over [0,T] if
\int_0^T
F(t)\dot x(t)\,dt
\le
E_{\mathrm{initial}}
for all admissible motions.
A memoryless damper satisfying
F_d\dot x\le0
is instantaneously dissipative and therefore passive.

11.5 Base-Excited Oscillator
A suspension is often excited by motion of its base rather
than by a direct applied force.

 Let:
• z(t) be sprung-mass displacement;
• y(t) be base or road displacement;
• r=z-y be relative suspension displacement.
The equation is
m\ddot z
+
c(\dot z-\dot y)
+
k(z-y)
=
0.
In relative coordinates,
m\ddot r
+
c\dot r
+
kr
=
-m\ddot y.
The road acceleration therefore acts as an effective forcing
term.

11.6 Energy Input from Base
Motion

 Define relative mechanical energy
E_r
=
\frac12m\dot r^2
+
\frac12kr^2.
Multiply the relative equation by \dot r:
\frac{dE_r}{dt}
+
c\dot r^2
=
-m\ddot y\,\dot r.

Proposition 11.3 — Base excitation is the
energy source
The mechanical input power into the relative suspension
mode is
P_{\mathrm{road}}
=
-m\ddot y\,\dot r.

Proof
It is the forcing term multiplied by generalized velocity. ∎
Any harvested energy ultimately originates from road
excitation, body motion, actuator input, gravitational

 potential change, propulsion energy, or another identifiable
mechanical source.

11.7 Electromagnetic Transducer
Consider a linear electromagnetic transducer with:
• mechanical velocity v;
• electrical current i;
• force constant k_f;
• back-EMF constant k_e.
Assume
F_{\mathrm{em}}
=
-k_f i
and
e
=
k_e v.
In consistent SI units for an ideal reciprocal transducer,
k_f=k_e=k_t.

11.8 Electromechanical Power
Reciprocity

 Mechanical power entering the transducer is
P_{\mathrm{mech}\rightarrow\mathrm{trans}}
=
-k_fiv
when the force opposes motion.
Electrical power generated by the induced voltage is
P_{\mathrm{emf}}
=
ei
=
k_evi.

Theorem 11.4 — Ideal power reciprocity
If
k_f=k_e=k_t,
then
ei
=
-k_{\!f}iv
up to the selected force and current sign convention.
Therefore mechanical power extracted from the motion
equals electrical power entering the electrical port before
losses.

 Proof
Substitute
e=k_tv
and
F_{\mathrm{em}}=-k_ti.
Then
ei=k_tvi
and
-F_{\mathrm{em}}v=k_tiv.
∎
The equality expresses energy conversion, not energy
multiplication.

11.9 Electrical Load Model
Let the coil have resistance R_c, inductance L_c, and
external load R_L.
The electrical equation is
L_c\dot i
+
(R_c+R_L)i

 =
k_ev.
Electrical stored energy is
E_L
=
\frac12L_ci^2.
Multiply the electrical equation by i:
L_ci\dot i
+
(R_c+R_L)i^2
=
k_evi.
Therefore
\frac{dE_L}{dt}
+
R_ci^2
+
R_Li^2
=
k_evi.

Theorem 11.5 — Electrical energy balance
\boxed{
\frac{dE_L}{dt}
+

 P_{\mathrm{coil\,loss}}
+
P_{\mathrm{load}}
=
P_{\mathrm{converted}}
}
with
P_{\mathrm{coil\,loss}}=R_ci^2,
P_{\mathrm{load}}=R_Li^2,
and
P_{\mathrm{converted}}=k_evi.

Proof
Directly from the multiplied circuit equation. ∎

11.10 Combined Electromechanical
Energy Balance
Consider the mechanical equation
m\ddot x
+
kx
+
c_m\dot x

 +
k_ti
=
F_{\mathrm{ext}},
and electrical equation
L\dot i
+
Ri
=
k_t\dot x,
where R=R_c+R_L.
Define total stored energy
E
=
\frac12m\dot x^2
+
\frac12kx^2
+
\frac12Li^2.
Multiply the mechanical equation by \dot x and the electrical
equation by i, then add.
The conversion terms
k_ti\dot x
cancel.

 Theorem 11.6 — Total electromechanical
conservation law
\boxed{
\frac{dE}{dt}
=
F_{\mathrm{ext}}\dot x
c_m\dot x^2
Ri^2
}

Proof
Mechanical energy gives
\frac{d}{dt}
\left(
\frac12m\dot x^2+\frac12kx^2
\right)
=
F_{\mathrm{ext}}\dot x
c_m\dot x^2
k_ti\dot x.
Electrical energy gives

 \frac{d}{dt}
\left(
\frac12Li^2
\right)
=
k_ti\dot x
Ri^2.
Adding cancels the internal conversion term. ∎
This is the central energy identity for an ideal reciprocal
linear generator.

11.11 Quasi-Static Electrical
Approximation
If electrical inductance is negligible over the mechanical
timescale,
L\dot i\approx0.
Then
i
=
\frac{k_tv}{R_c+R_L}.
The electromagnetic force becomes

 F_{\mathrm{em}}
=
-k_ti
=
\frac{k_t^2}{R_c+R_L}v.
Define equivalent electromagnetic damping
c_e
=
\frac{k_t^2}{R_c+R_L}.
Thus
F_{\mathrm{em}}=-c_ev.

Theorem 11.7 — Resistive electrical loading
appears as mechanical damping
Under the quasi-static approximation,
\boxed{
c_e
=
\frac{k_t^2}{R_c+R_L}
}
and the transducer acts as a viscous damper.

Proof

 Substitute the resistive current into the force law. ∎

11.12 Harvested Load Power
The load power is
P_L
=
i^2R_L.
Using
i
=
\frac{k_tv}{R_c+R_L},
P_L
=
\frac{k_t^2v^2R_L}
{(R_c+R_L)^2}.
The coil loss is
P_c
=
\frac{k_t^2v^2R_c}
{(R_c+R_L)^2}.
Total electromagnetic mechanical extraction is
P_{\mathrm{mech,ext}}
=

 c_ev^2
=
\frac{k_t^2v^2}
{R_c+R_L}.
And indeed,
P_{\mathrm{mech,ext}}
=
P_L+P_c.

11.13 Electrical Conversion
Efficiency
Define instantaneous conversion efficiency from extracted
mechanical power to useful load power:
\eta_e
=
\frac{P_L}{P_L+P_c}.
Substituting,
\eta_e
=
\frac{R_L}{R_c+R_L}.

Proposition 11.8 — Resistive conversion
efficiency

 \boxed{
\eta_e
=
\frac{R_L}{R_c+R_L}
}

Proof
Cancel the common factor
k_t^2v^2/(R_c+R_L)^2.
∎
Large R_L improves electrical efficiency but reduces current
and mechanical damping.

11.14 Maximum Load Power for
Prescribed Velocity
Assume the mechanical velocity v is externally prescribed
and unaffected by electrical loading.
Then
P_L(R_L)
=
\frac{k_t^2v^2R_L}
{(R_c+R_L)^2}.
Differentiate:

 \frac{dP_L}{dR_L}
=
k_t^2v^2
\frac{
R_c-R_L
}{
(R_c+R_L)^3
}.

Theorem 11.9 — Resistive impedance
matching
For prescribed velocity, load power is maximized when
\boxed{R_L=R_c}.
At the optimum,
P_{L,\max}
=
\frac{k_t^2v^2}{4R_c}.

Proof
The derivative vanishes at R_L=R_c. It is positive below and
negative above this value. ∎
At maximum electrical power transfer, half of the converted
power is lost in the coil:
\eta_e=\frac12.

 11.15 Why Maximum-Power
Matching Can Fail in a Coupled
Suspension
In a real harvester, velocity is not fixed independently of
R_L.
Changing load resistance changes damping:
c_e(R_L)
=
\frac{k_t^2}{R_c+R_L},
which changes the mechanical response amplitude and
therefore changes v.
Thus the actual optimization is
P_L(R_L)
=
\frac{k_t^2R_L}
{(R_c+R_L)^2}
v(R_L)^2.
The optimum need not satisfy
R_L=R_c.

 Proposition 11.10 — Coupled optimum
depends on mechanical dynamics
When velocity depends on load,
\frac{dP_L}{dR_L}
contains both the direct electrical derivative and the
derivative of v(R_L).

Proof
Apply the product rule:
\frac{dP_L}{dR_L}
=
\frac{\partial P_L}{\partial R_L}
+
\frac{\partial P_L}{\partial v}
\frac{dv}{dR_L}.
The second term generally does not vanish. ∎
Maximum-power transfer must be optimized on the coupled
system.

11.16 Harmonic Base Excitation
Let
y(t)=Y\cos\omega t.

 For the base-excited relative equation
m\ddot r+c_t\dot r+kr=-m\ddot y,
where
c_t=c_m+c_e,
the forcing amplitude is
m\omega^2Y.
The steady-state relative-displacement amplitude is
R(\omega)
=
\frac{
m\omega^2Y
}{
\sqrt{
(k-m\omega^2)^2
+
(c_t\omega)^2
}
}.
Relative-velocity amplitude is
V_r=\omega R.

11.17 Mean Harvested Power Under
Harmonic Motion

 For sinusoidal relative velocity
v(t)=V_r\cos(\omega t-\phi),
the mean-square velocity is
\langle v^2\rangle
=
\frac{V_r^2}{2}.
The mean load power is
\overline P_L
=
\frac12
\frac{
k_t^2R_L
}{
(R_c+R_L)^2
}
V_r^2.
Substituting V_r,
\overline P_L
=
\frac12
\frac{
k_t^2R_L
}{
(R_c+R_L)^2
}

 \frac{
m^2\omega^6Y^2
}{
(k-m\omega^2)^2
+
(c_t\omega)^2
}.
This equation displays the central trade-off:
• increasing electrical damping improves conversion
coefficient;
• but excessive damping reduces relative velocity.

11.18 Optimal Total Damping at
Resonance
At mechanical resonance,
k=m\omega^2,
so
V_r
=
\frac{m\omega^3Y}{c_t\omega}
=
\frac{m\omega^2Y}{c_t}.
The mean power extracted by electromagnetic damping is

 \overline P_e
=
\frac12c_eV_r^2
=
\frac12
c_e
\frac{
m^2\omega^4Y^2
}{
(c_m+c_e)^2
}.
Treating c_m as fixed, maximize
f(c_e)
=
\frac{c_e}{(c_m+c_e)^2}.
Differentiate:
f'(c_e)
=
\frac{
c_m-c_e
}{
(c_m+c_e)^3
}.

Theorem 11.11 — Damping match at ideal
resonance

 For a harmonically base-excited linear oscillator at exact
resonance, total electromagnetic extraction is maximized
when
\boxed{c_e=c_m}.

Proof
The derivative changes from positive to negative at
c_e=c_m. ∎
This is the mechanical analogue of matching loss channels.
Useful load power is lower than total electromagnetic
extraction because coil losses must be subtracted.

11.19 Suspension Comfort Versus
Harvesting
In a vehicle, maximizing relative suspension velocity may
conflict with ride comfort.
Representative objectives include:
• sprung-mass acceleration;
• suspension travel;
• dynamic tire load;
• harvested power.
Define a multi-objective cost

 J
=
w_a
\int a_s^2dt
+
w_r
\int r^2dt
+
w_t
\int F_t^2dt
w_p
\int P_Ldt.
The negative sign on harvested power rewards energy
recovery.
Different weights produce different compromises.

Proposition 11.12 — No universal optimum
without an objective
A damping law cannot be called globally optimal unless the
performance functional, constraints, excitation distribution,
and operating regime are specified.

Proof
Different objectives can rank the same candidate controllers
differently. ∎

 Maximum energy harvesting and best ride quality are
generally not identical goals.

11.20 Quarter-Car Suspension
Model
Let:
• m_s be sprung mass;
• m_u be unsprung mass;
• z_s be sprung displacement;
• z_u be unsprung displacement;
• z_r be road input;
• k_s be suspension stiffness;
• c_s be suspension damping;
• k_t be tire stiffness.
The equations are
m_s\ddot z_s
=
-k_s(z_s-z_u)
-c_s(\dot z_s-\dot z_u)
+
F_a,
m_u\ddot z_u
=
k_s(z_s-z_u)
+

 c_s(\dot z_s-\dot z_u)
k_t(z_u-z_r)
F_a.
Here F_a is an actuator or regenerative force applied
internally between the masses.

11.21 Internal Force Cancellation
Lemma 11.13 — Suspension actuator
conserves total mechanical momentum
internally
Adding the two equations cancels F_a:
m_s\ddot z_s+m_u\ddot z_u
=
-k_t(z_u-z_r).

Proof
The actuator acts with equal and opposite forces on the two
masses. ∎
An internal suspension actuator redistributes motion between
sprung and unsprung masses; it does not create net external
momentum.

 11.22 Quarter-Car Stored Energy
Define
E_q
=
\frac12m_s\dot z_s^2
+
\frac12m_u\dot z_u^2
+
\frac12k_s(z_s-z_u)^2
+
\frac12k_t(z_u-z_r)^2.
Because the road coordinate is time varying, differentiating
the tire energy introduces road-input power.
Let
v_r=\dot z_s-\dot z_u.
The passive damper power is
-c_sv_r^2.
The actuator power transferred into the mechanical
suspension is
P_a
=
F_av_r.

 Theorem 11.14 — Quarter-car energy
balance
\frac{dE_q}{dt}
=
-c_sv_r^2
+
F_av_r
k_t(z_u-z_r)\dot z_r.

Proof
Multiply each mass equation by its corresponding velocity,
add, and differentiate the spring energies. ∎
The road-input power is
P_{\mathrm{road}}
=
-k_t(z_u-z_r)\dot z_r.
The actuator is regenerative when
F_av_r<0.

11.23 Regenerative Force Sign
Definition 11.2 — Instantaneously
regenerative force

 A suspension force is instantaneously regenerative if
P_a=F_av_r<0.
The extracted mechanical power is
P_{\mathrm{ext}}=-F_av_r>0.
A force may improve ride while consuming energy when
F_av_r>0.
Thus active control and regeneration are not synonymous.

11.24 Semi-Active Damping
Constraint
A semi-active damper cannot supply net mechanical energy.
Its force must satisfy
F_{\mathrm{sa}}v_r\le0.
A variable-damping law has form
F_{\mathrm{sa}}
=
-c(t)v_r,
with

 c_{\min}\le c(t)\le c_{\max},
\qquad
c_{\min}\ge0.
Then
F_{\mathrm{sa}}v_r
=
-c(t)v_r^2
\le0.

Theorem 11.15 — Passivity of bounded
variable damping
Any damping law
F=-c(t,x,\dot x)\dot x
with
c(t,x,\dot x)\ge0
is instantaneously dissipative.

Proof
F\dot x
=
-c(t,x,\dot x)\dot x^2
\le0.
∎

 The coefficient may be nonlinear, state dependent, or time
varying without violating passivity, provided it remains
nonnegative.

11.25 Skyhook Damping
An ideal skyhook controller applies force approximately
proportional to sprung-mass absolute velocity:
F_{\mathrm{sky}}
=
-c_{\mathrm{sky}}\dot z_s.
A physical suspension actuator acts between the two masses,
so the desired force is implemented conditionally or
approximately.
A common semi-active logic selects high damping when the
available damper force opposes sprung-mass motion:
\dot z_s
(\dot z_s-\dot z_u)>0.
Otherwise, low damping is selected.

11.26 Passivity Projection
Suppose an active controller requests force
F_d.

 To enforce semi-active behavior, project it onto the
dissipative force set.
For relative velocity v_r\neq0, require
Fv_r\le0.
With force bound |F|\le F_{\max}, the admissible interval is:
F\in[-F_{\max},0]
when v_r>0, and
F\in[0,F_{\max}]
when v_r<0.

Proposition 11.16 — Closest passive force
The Euclidean projection of F_d onto the admissible interval
gives the minimum-change passive approximation.

Proof
Projection onto a closed convex interval uniquely minimizes
squared distance to F_d. ∎
This provides a rigorous safety layer around an
unconstrained controller.

11.27 Clipped-Optimal Regenerative
Control

 Suppose an unconstrained optimal-control law requests
F^*(t).
A regenerative implementation may use
F_{\mathrm{regen}}
=
\Pi_{\mathcal F(v_r)}
(F^*),
where
\mathcal F(v_r)
=
\{F:Fv_r\le0,\ |F|\le F_{\max}\}.
This preserves the requested force whenever it is already
regenerative and clips it otherwise.

11.28 Active Suspension Power
An active actuator may draw electrical power
P_{\mathrm{elec,in}}
while delivering mechanical power
P_{\mathrm{mech}}
=
F_av_r.
Under motoring operation,

 P_{\mathrm{mech}}>0.
Under regeneration,
P_{\mathrm{mech}}<0.
A bidirectional power converter can exchange energy with
storage in both directions.

11.29 Bidirectional Efficiency
Let \eta_m be motoring efficiency and \eta_g be generating
efficiency.
For motoring:
P_{\mathrm{elec,in}}
=
\frac{
P_{\mathrm{mech,out}}
}{
\eta_m
}.
For generation:
P_{\mathrm{elec,out}}
=
\eta_g
P_{\mathrm{mech,in}}.
Both satisfy

 0<\eta_m,\eta_g\le1.
Round-trip efficiency is
\eta_{\mathrm{rt}}
=
\eta_m\eta_g
before storage losses.

11.30 Net Energy Recovery
Over interval [0,T], define generated electrical energy
E_g
=
\int_0^T
\max(0,-F_av_r)\eta_g\,dt.
Define consumed actuator energy
E_c
=
\int_0^T
\frac{
\max(0,F_av_r)
}{
\eta_m
}
\,dt.
Auxiliary electronics consume energy E_{\mathrm{aux}}.

 Net recovery is
E_{\mathrm{net}}
=
E_g-E_c-E_{\mathrm{aux}}.
A regenerative suspension can have positive gross generation
but negative net energy after actuation and electronics.

11.31 Energy-Neutral Control
Definition 11.3 — Energy-neutral operating
horizon
The controller is energy neutral over [0,T] if
E_g
\ge
E_c+E_{\mathrm{aux}}.
This is a horizon-based statement, not an instantaneous one.
A controller may consume energy during one event and
recover it during another.

11.32 Storage Dynamics
Let storage energy be E_b.
A simplified model is

 \dot E_b
=
\eta_cP_{\mathrm{charge}}
\frac{
P_{\mathrm{discharge}}
}{
\eta_d
}
P_{\mathrm{self}},
with bounds
E_{\min}
\le
E_b
\le
E_{\max}.
A controller requesting regeneration when storage is full
must divert or dissipate the energy elsewhere.

11.33 State-of-Charge Constraint
Let normalized state of charge be
s=\frac{E_b-E_{\min}}{E_{\max}-E_{\min}}.
Then

 0\le s\le1.
A constrained controller must satisfy forward invariance of
this interval.
For example, at s=1,
\dot s\le0,
and at s=0,
\dot s\ge0.

Theorem 11.17 — Interval invariance
condition
For scalar storage state s\in[0,1], if
f(0,u)\ge0
and
f(1,u)\le0
for every admissible boundary control, then solutions cannot
leave the interval through either boundary under standard
uniqueness assumptions.

Proof
At the lower boundary, the vector field does not point
outward. At the upper boundary, it also does not point

 outward. This is the one-dimensional tangent-cone condition
for invariance. ∎

11.34 Heave Natural Frequency
For a single sprung mass with effective suspension stiffness
k_s,
\omega_h
=
\sqrt{\frac{k_s}{m_s}},
and
f_h
=
\frac1{2\pi}
\sqrt{\frac{k_s}{m_s}}.
This is the ideal undamped heave frequency.

11.35 Wheel-Hop Frequency
Ignoring coupling for a first approximation, unsprung wheelhop frequency is
\omega_w
\approx
\sqrt{

 \frac{k_t+k_s}{m_u}
}.
Because m_u\ll m_s and k_t is high, wheel-hop frequency is
typically higher than body heave frequency.
Exact normal frequencies follow from the coupled
eigenvalue problem.

11.36 Quarter-Car Eigenvalue
Problem
For the undamped fixed-road system,
M\ddot q+Kq=0,
with
q
=
\begin{bmatrix}
z_s\\z_u
\end{bmatrix},
M
=
\begin{bmatrix}
m_s&0\\
0&m_u
\end{bmatrix},

 and
K
=
\begin{bmatrix}
k_s&-k_s\\
-k_s&k_s+k_t
\end{bmatrix}.
Normal frequencies satisfy
\det(K-\omega^2M)=0.

Theorem 11.18 — Quarter-car characteristic
equation
m_sm_u\omega^4
\left[
m_s(k_s+k_t)+m_uk_s
\right]\omega^2
+
k_sk_t
=
0.

Proof
Compute the determinant:

 \det
\begin{bmatrix}
k_s-m_s\omega^2&-k_s\\
-k_s&k_s+k_t-m_u\omega^2
\end{bmatrix}
=0.
Expanding and simplifying gives the polynomial. ∎
Its two positive roots correspond approximately to body
heave and wheel hop.

11.37 Positivity of Quarter-Car
Frequencies
Assume
m_s,m_u,k_s,k_t>0.
The quadratic in \lambda=\omega^2 has:
• positive sum of roots;
• positive product of roots.
Its discriminant is nonnegative because the generalized
stiffness problem has real eigenvalues.
Therefore both squared frequencies are positive.

11.38 Damped State-Space Model

 Define state
x
=
\begin{bmatrix}
z_s-z_u\\
z_u-z_r\\
\dot z_s\\
\dot z_u
\end{bmatrix}.
Then
\dot x=Ax+B_uu+B_rw,
where:
• u=F_a;
• w represents road velocity or acceleration, depending on
state definition.
This form supports linear control, estimation, and
optimization.
The exact matrices must be derived consistently from the
chosen coordinates.

11.39 Controllability
For
\dot x=Ax+Bu,

 the controllability matrix is
\mathcal C
=
\begin{bmatrix}
B&AB&A^2B&\cdots&A^{n-1}B
\end{bmatrix}.
The system is controllable if
\operatorname{rank}\mathcal C=n.
A suspension actuator may fail to control a mode if its force
direction is orthogonal to that mode in generalized
coordinates.

11.40 Observability
With measurements
y=Cx,
the observability matrix is
\mathcal O
=
\begin{bmatrix}
C\\
CA\\
CA^2\\
\vdots\\

 CA^{n-1}
\end{bmatrix}.
The state is observable if
\operatorname{rank}\mathcal O=n.
A controller requiring unmeasured suspension velocity must
use sensing, differentiation, or an observer.

11.41 Linear Quadratic Control
For
\dot x=Ax+Bu,
define cost
J
=
\int_0^\infty
\left(
x^TQx+u^TRu
\right)dt,
with
Q\succeq0,
\qquad
R\succ0.
The optimal state feedback is

 u=-Kx,
where
K=R^{-1}B^TP
and P solves the algebraic Riccati equation
A^TP+PA-PBR^{-1}B^TP+Q=0.
This controller generally consumes energy and is not
automatically regenerative.

11.42 Regeneration-Aware Optimal
Control
Include electrical power or storage energy in the objective:
J
=
\int
\left[
x^TQx
+
u^TRu
\lambda P_{\mathrm{regen}}(x,u)
\right]dt.
Because

 P_{\mathrm{regen}}
=
-\min(0,uv_r)
is nonsmooth, practical formulations may introduce auxiliary
variables or piecewise models.
The resulting controller balances ride and energy recovery
explicitly.

11.43 Passivity-Based Control
Let a mechanical system have storage function H(x)
satisfying
\dot H
=
y^Tu
D(x),
\qquad
D(x)\ge0.
If feedback is
u=-Ky,
\qquad
K\succeq0,
then

 \dot H
=
-y^TKy-D(x)
\le0.

Theorem 11.19 — Passive output feedback
stability
If H is positive definite and radially unbounded, and the
largest invariant set in
\{\dot H=0\}
is the equilibrium, then the equilibrium is asymptotically
stable.

Proof
The storage function is a Lyapunov function. Apply
LaSalle’s invariance principle. ∎
This provides a strong route to safe damping control.

11.44 Port-Hamiltonian Form
An electromechanical suspension may be written
\dot z
=
[J(z)-R(z)]
\nabla H(z)

 +
G(z)u,
where:
• J^T=-J represents energy-conserving interconnection;
• R\succeq0 represents dissipation;
• H is stored energy;
• u is external input.
Then
\dot H
=
-\nabla H^TR\nabla H
+
y^Tu,
with
y=G^T\nabla H.
This structure exposes conservation and dissipation directly.

11.45 Skew-Symmetric
Interconnection
Lemma 11.20
For any vector g and skew-symmetric matrix J,
g^TJg=0.

 Proof
g^TJg
=
(g^TJg)^T
=
g^TJ^Tg
=
-g^TJg.
Therefore the scalar equals its negative and must be zero. ∎
The J-term redistributes energy but does not create or destroy
it.

11.46 Mechanical Impedance
For harmonic motion with phasor velocity V, mechanical
impedance is
Z_m(\omega)
=
\frac F V.
For a mass–spring–damper,
Z_m(\omega)
=
c
+
i

 \left(
\omega m-\frac{k}{\omega}
\right).
At resonance,
\omega m-\frac{k}{\omega}=0,
so the impedance is purely resistive:
Z_m=c.

11.47 Electrical Reflection into
Mechanical Impedance
The transducer with electrical impedance
Z_e(\omega)
reflects a mechanical impedance
Z_{\mathrm{em}}(\omega)
=
\frac{k_t^2}{Z_e(\omega)}
under the chosen sign convention.
If
Z_e=R+iX,
then

 Z_{\mathrm{em}}
=
k_t^2
\frac{R-iX}{R^2+X^2}.
Its real part gives damping:
c_e(\omega)
=
k_t^2
\frac{R}{R^2+X^2}.
Its imaginary part modifies apparent stiffness or inertia.

11.48 Inductive Roll-Off
For
Z_e=R+i\omega L,
the reflected damping is
c_e(\omega)
=
\frac{k_t^2R}
{R^2+\omega^2L^2}.
At low frequency,
c_e\approx\frac{k_t^2}{R}.
At high frequency,

 c_e\sim
\frac{k_t^2R}{\omega^2L^2}.
Thus coil inductance reduces high-frequency damping and
harvesting.

11.49 Reactive Compensation
A capacitor can compensate coil inductance near a target
frequency.
For series electrical impedance,
Z_e
=
R+i
\left(
\omega L-\frac1{\omega C}
\right).
At electrical resonance,
\omega L=\frac1{\omega C},
so
Z_e=R
and reflected damping is maximized for that resistance.
Reactive compensation changes bandwidth and voltage stress
and must be analyzed with parasitics.

 11.50 Adjustable Damping Through
Power Electronics
A controlled converter can emulate an effective resistance
R_{\mathrm{eff}}(t)
at the generator terminals.
Then
c_e(t)
\approx
\frac{k_t^2}{R_c+R_{\mathrm{eff}}(t)}
in the quasi-static regime.
This enables semi-active damping without physically
changing the transducer.
The converter still has switching and conduction losses.

11.51 Negative Resistance Boundary
If the converter emulates
R_{\mathrm{eff}}<-R_c,
the denominator becomes negative and
c_e<0.

 The transducer then injects mechanical energy rather than
harvesting it.
This is active behavior and can destabilize the suspension.

Theorem 11.21 — Negative damping
instability of a simple oscillator
For
m\ddot x+c_t +kx=0,
if
c_t<0,
the equilibrium is unstable.

Proof
The characteristic equation is
m\lambda^2+c_t\lambda+k=0.
The sum of roots is
-\frac{c_t}{m}>0.
Therefore at least one root has positive real part. ∎

ẋ

Active negative damping requires additional stabilizing
control.

 11.52 Saturation
Real regenerative force is bounded:
|F_a|
\le
F_{\max}.
Generator current is bounded:
|i|
\le
I_{\max}.
Since
F_a=k_ti,
the current limit gives
|F_a|
\le
k_tI_{\max}.
Voltage limits also constrain force at high speed because
e=k_tv.

11.53 Voltage-Limited Regeneration
For a DC bus with allowable converter voltage V_{\max},

 |k_tv-L\dot i-R_ci|
\le
V_{\max}.
At high velocity, back EMF may exceed converter voltage
capability, limiting current control.
Field weakening or alternative winding configurations may
be needed, each with trade-offs.

11.54 Force–Velocity Feasible
Region
A simple quasi-static electrical relation is
V
=
k_tv-R_ci.
With
F=k_ti,
V
=
k_tv-\frac{R_c}{k_t}F.
Voltage and current limits define a feasible region in the (v,F)
plane.
A requested damping law outside this region cannot be
realized.

 11.55 Harvested Power Bound
Under current limit,
|i|\le I_{\max},
the instantaneous electrical conversion power satisfies
|P_{\mathrm{conv}}|
=
|k_tvi|
\le
k_t|v|I_{\max}.
Under force limit,
|F|\le F_{\max},
mechanical extraction obeys
P_{\mathrm{ext}}
\le
F_{\max}|v|.
These are actuator-envelope bounds.

11.56 Cauchy–Schwarz Energy
Bound
Over a horizon [0,T],

 E_h
=
\int_0^T
c_e(t)v(t)^2dt.
If
0\le c_e(t)\le c_{\max},
then
E_h
\le
c_{\max}
\int_0^T v(t)^2dt.
Thus harvested mechanical energy is bounded by the
velocity-energy content of suspension motion.

11.57 Road-Input Upper Bound
From the energy balance,
E_{\mathrm{harvested}}
+
E_{\mathrm{other\,loss}}
=
E_{\mathrm{road\,input}}
\Delta E_{\mathrm{stored}}
over a horizon.

 Therefore
E_{\mathrm{harvested}}
\le
E_{\mathrm{road\,input}}
+
E_{\mathrm{initial\,stored}}
when final stored energy is nonnegative.
No passive suspension can harvest more energy than enters
from excitation plus released initial storage.

Theorem 11.22 — Passive harvesting upper
bound
For a passive system beginning with stored energy E(0)\ge0,
E_{\mathrm{useful,out}}(T)
\le
E_{\mathrm{external,in}}(T)+E(0).

Proof
Integrate the total energy balance. All dissipative losses and
final stored energy are nonnegative. ∎
This excludes sustained energy-positive operation without a
corresponding external energy source.

11.58 Terrain Energy Source

 A vehicle traversing rough terrain exchanges energy among:
• propulsion system;
• vehicle kinetic energy;
• gravitational potential;
• suspension storage;
• tire deformation;
• terrain deformation;
• thermal dissipation.
Harvesting suspension motion may slightly increase the
propulsion energy required to maintain speed because added
damping resists motion induced by the terrain.
The full vehicle-energy balance must include this effect.

11.59 Constant-Speed Propulsion
Penalty
If suspension harvesting adds mean resisting force projected
along vehicle travel,
\overline F_{\mathrm{res}},
then maintaining speed V_x requires additional propulsion
power approximately
P_{\mathrm{prop,extra}}
=
\overline F_{\mathrm{res}}V_x.

 This quantity may exceed, equal, or be less than recovered
electrical power depending on the mechanical pathways and
efficiency.
A suspension harvester can still be valuable for damping and
recovering energy that would otherwise become heat, but it
cannot be evaluated from generator output alone.

11.60 Regeneration Versus Added
Drag
Proposition 11.23
Positive electrical generation does not prove reduced total
vehicle-energy consumption.

Proof
The generator may increase mechanical resistance, causing
the traction system to supply additional energy. Net benefit
requires comparing recovered energy with added propulsion
and conversion losses. ∎
The correct metric is vehicle-level net energy, not isolated
generator output.

11.61 Random Road Input

 Road profiles are often modeled as stochastic processes with
power spectral density
S_r(\omega).
For a linear system with transfer function from road input to
relative velocity
H_v(\omega),
the relative-velocity spectrum is
S_v(\omega)
=
|H_v(\omega)|^2S_r(\omega).
Mean-square velocity is
\mathbb E[v^2]
=
\frac1{2\pi}
\int_{-\infty}^{\infty}
S_v(\omega)\,d\omega.

11.62 Mean Harvested Power Under
Stationary Random Excitation
For constant effective damping c_e,
\overline P_e
=
c_e\mathbb E[v^2].

 Therefore
\overline P_e
=
\frac{c_e}{2\pi}
\int
|H_v(\omega;c_e)|^2
S_r(\omega)\,d\omega.
Because H_v depends on c_e, maximizing average power
requires optimizing the full integral.

11.63 Stochastic Optimization
Let road spectra vary with road class and speed.
Define expected objective
J(c_e)
=
\mathbb E_{\rho}
\left[
w_pP_h
w_aA_s
w_tT_d
\right],
where \rho indexes operating conditions.

 A robust damping law maximizes expected or worst-case
performance over a specified distribution or uncertainty set.
A controller optimized on one road profile may perform
poorly elsewhere.

11.64 Adaptive Damping
Let the damping coefficient be adjusted according to
estimated state:
c_e(t)
=
\pi(\hat x(t)).
To retain passivity, enforce
0\le c_e(t)\le c_{\max}.
Then instantaneous extracted mechanical power is
P_e=c_e(t)v_r^2\ge0.
The electrical useful output remains
P_L=\eta_e(t)P_e
after conversion loss.

11.65 Estimation Error
Suppose estimated relative velocity is

 \hat v=v+\varepsilon_v.
A requested force
F=-c\hat v
has true mechanical power
P
=
Fv
=
-cv^2-c\varepsilon_vv.
The second term may be positive enough to violate passivity.

Theorem 11.24 — Robust passivity condition
with bounded velocity error
Assume
|\varepsilon_v|\le\bar\varepsilon.
For force
F=-c\hat v,
a sufficient condition for
Fv\le0
is
|\hat v|\ge\bar\varepsilon

 and force sign chosen to oppose every true velocity
consistent with the estimate.

Explanation
When the uncertainty interval for v includes both signs, no
nonzero force based only on \hat v can guarantee opposition
to the true motion. A safe controller may set force to zero or
minimum damping in that region.

11.66 Passivity Observer
Define cumulative controller energy exchange
E_c(t)
=
\int_0^t
F_a(\tau)v_r(\tau)\,d\tau.
A passive controller should not allow cumulative supplied
energy to exceed an allowed energy tank.
A passivity observer tracks E_c, and a passivity controller
modifies commands when the energy budget would be
violated.

11.67 Energy Tank
Let E_T\ge0 be a virtual stored-energy state:

 \dot E_T
=
-P_a-P_{\mathrm{loss}},
under a selected convention.
Active action is permitted only when sufficient tank energy
exists.
Regenerative events refill the tank.

Theorem 11.25 — Passivity with a
nonnegative energy tank
If:
1. total storage is
H_{\mathrm{tot}}=H_{\mathrm{plant}}+E_T;
2. the tank is constrained by
E_T\ge0;
3. active power is drawn only from E_T;
then the combined plant–controller system remains passive
relative to external ports, assuming all internal accounting is
exact.

Proof
Active controller output decreases E_T by the same amount
it increases plant energy. Internal exchange cancels in the
total storage derivative. Nonnegative dissipation remains. ∎

 This is a formal method for mixing active ride control with
previously recovered energy.

11.68 Magnetic Spring Force
A nonlinear magnetic spring may have potential
U_m(x),
with force
F_m(x)
=
-\frac{dU_m}{dx}.
Its tangent stiffness is
k_m(x)
=
\frac{d^2U_m}{dx^2}.
Local stability at equilibrium x_* requires
U_m'(x_*)=0
and
U_m''(x_*)>0.

11.69 Negative Stiffness
A magnetic arrangement may exhibit a region where

 k_m(x)<0.
Negative stiffness can reduce effective suspension stiffness
when combined with a positive mechanical spring.
Total tangent stiffness is
k_{\mathrm{tot}}
=
k_s+k_m.
Local static stability requires
k_{\mathrm{tot}}>0.

Theorem 11.26 — Static instability under
negative total stiffness
For potential U near equilibrium,
U(x_*+\delta)
=
U(x_*)
+
\frac12k_{\mathrm{tot}}\delta^2
+
o(\delta^2).
If
k_{\mathrm{tot}}<0,
the equilibrium is not a local minimum.

 Proof
Small nonzero \delta lowers the potential. ∎
Negative stiffness must be bounded and stabilized by
positive stiffness or control.

11.70 Progressive Magnetic Spring
A progressive spring has increasing tangent stiffness:
\frac{dk_m}{dx}>0
over the operating range, or more generally stiffness
magnitude grows with displacement.
For a polynomial potential
U(x)
=
\frac12k_2x^2
+
\frac14k_4x^4,
\qquad
k_2,k_4>0,
force is
F=-k_2x-k_4x^3,
and tangent stiffness is

 k_{\mathrm{tan}}
=
k_2+3k_4x^2>0.
This yields soft central response and stronger end-stroke
resistance.

11.71 Nonlinear Damping
A nonlinear damper may satisfy
F_d
=
-c_1v-c_3v^3,
with
c_1,c_3\ge0.
Power is
P_d
=
F_dv
=
-c_1v^2-c_3v^4
\le0.

Proposition 11.27 — Passivity of odd
monotone damping
Any force law

 F_d=-g(v)
with
vg(v)\ge0
is dissipative.

Proof
F_dv=-vg(v)\le0.
∎

11.72 Hysteretic Damping
If force depends on internal hysteresis state h,
F=F(x,v,h),
instantaneous force–velocity sign may not always be
nonpositive because energy can be temporarily stored and
returned.
Passivity must then be tested with an augmented storage
function
H(x,h).
A loop area in the force–displacement plane represents net
energy dissipated per cycle:

 E_{\mathrm{cycle}}
=
\oint F\,dx.
The sign depends on the plotting convention.

11.73 Eddy-Current Damping
For a conductor moving through a magnetic field at
sufficiently low speed, induced current can produce
approximately viscous force:
F_e=-cv.
At higher speed or frequency, skin effect, inductance,
geometry, and field nonuniformity make the damping
frequency dependent.
The electrical energy is primarily dissipated as heat unless
the induced current is routed into a useful load.
Eddy-current damping alone is not necessarily regenerative.

11.74 Piezoelectric Harvester Model
A simplified piezoelectric transducer can be written
F=kx+\theta v_p,
q=\theta x+C_pv_p,
where:

 • v_p is electrical voltage;
• q is charge;
• \theta is coupling coefficient;
• C_p is capacitance.
The reciprocal coupling coefficient appears in both
mechanical and electrical equations under a consistent
energy formulation.

11.75 Piezoelectric Stored Energy
A quadratic electromechanical energy may be written
H
=
\frac12kx^2
\theta xv_p
+
\frac12C_pv_p^2
under one choice of independent variables.
Positive definiteness requires
k>0,
\qquad
C_p>0,
\qquad
kC_p-\theta^2>0.

 Theorem 11.28 — Coupling stability
condition
The quadratic form
\frac12
\begin{bmatrix}
x&v_p
\end{bmatrix}
\begin{bmatrix}
k&-\theta\\
-\theta&C_p
\end{bmatrix}
\begin{bmatrix}
x\\v_p
\end{bmatrix}
is positive definite if and only if
k>0
and
kC_p-\theta^2>0.

Proof
Apply the positive-definite criterion for a symmetric
2\times2 matrix. ∎

 Too-strong coupling relative to the selected uncoupled
coefficients would make the assumed quadratic energy
unphysical.

11.76 Hydraulic Energy Recovery
For hydraulic pressure p and volumetric flow Q,
P_h=pQ.
An accumulator stores energy through fluid compression.
A hydraulic motor–generator may convert this flow into
electricity.
Losses include:
• pressure drop;
• leakage;
• throttling;
• pump/motor inefficiency;
• generator loss;
• accumulator hysteresis.
A throttling damper dissipates energy; a controlled hydraulic
circuit may recover part of it.

11.77 Rotary Conversion
A ball screw or rack mechanism may convert suspension
velocity v into generator speed

 \omega_g=Gv,
where G is a kinematic ratio with suitable units.
Generator torque \tau_g reflects mechanical force
F=G\tau_g
under ideal power preservation:
Fv=\tau_g\omega_g.
Friction, inertia, backlash, and screw efficiency modify these
relations.

11.78 Reflected Inertia
A rotary inertia J_g reflected through ratio G appears as
translational inertia
m_{\mathrm{ref}}
=
J_gG^2.

Proof
Rotary kinetic energy is
\frac12J_g\omega_g^2
=
\frac12J_gG^2v^2.
Equate to

 \frac12m_{\mathrm{ref}}v^2.
∎
High conversion ratios increase generator speed but also
increase reflected inertia quadratically.

11.79 Reflected Damping
A rotary damping torque
\tau=-b_g\omega_g
reflects as translational force
F=-G\tau
under sign convention, giving equivalent damping
c_{\mathrm{ref}}
=
b_gG^2.
Again, the ratio enters quadratically.

11.80 Mechanical Backlash
Boundary
Backlash creates a dead zone in which suspension motion
does not transmit continuously to the generator.
This introduces:

 • impact;
• hysteresis;
• noise;
• delayed damping;
• control nonlinearity.
A linear regenerative-damping model is invalid inside the
backlash transition unless augmented.

11.81 Fatigue and Harvesting
Energy recovery may increase force cycles or local stress.
For stress amplitude \sigma_a, fatigue life may be
approximated by an S-N relation
\sigma_a^mN=C
over a limited material regime.
A design maximizing recovered power but sharply reducing
fatigue life may be unacceptable.
Structural durability must be part of the objective or
constraints.

11.82 Thermal Limit of a Generator
Copper loss is
P_c=i_{\mathrm{rms}}^2R_c(T).

 Resistance varies approximately as
R_c(T)
=
R_0
\left[
1+\alpha(T-T_0)
\right].
Higher temperature increases loss, reducing allowable
continuous current.
A transient high-power event may be feasible even when
continuous operation is not.

11.83 Regenerative Damping
Coefficient Under Thermal Drift
Because
c_e
=
\frac{k_t^2}{R_c(T)+R_L},
increasing coil resistance reduces effective damping for a
fixed load.
Thus suspension behavior can drift with temperature unless
compensated.

 11.84 Fault Modes
A regenerative suspension should account for:
• open circuit;
• short circuit;
• converter failure;
• sensor failure;
• overtemperature;
• storage full;
• storage disconnected;
• communication loss;
• mechanical jam.
Open circuit gives approximately
i=0,
\qquad
c_e\approx0.
Short circuit gives high damping approximately
c_e\approx\frac{k_t^2}{R_c}
subject to inductance and current limits.
The safe mechanical behavior of both extremes must be
evaluated.

11.85 Fail-Safe Passive Mode

 A robust architecture may default to a passive damping path
upon loss of control.
If the fallback force satisfies
Fv_r\le0
and remains within structural limits, loss of computation
does not produce active instability.
This is an architectural safety property rather than a
performance guarantee.

11.86 Robust Stability with
Damping Uncertainty
Consider
m\ddot x+c\dot x+kx=0,
where
c\in[c_{\min},c_{\max}].
If
m>0,
\qquad
k>0,
\qquad
c_{\min}>0,

 then every member of the uncertainty family is
asymptotically stable.

Proof
The characteristic polynomial
m\lambda^2+c\lambda+k
has positive coefficients for every admissible c. The Routh–
Hurwitz criterion for a second-order polynomial gives
negative-real-part roots. ∎
If c_{\min}=0, the system may be neutrally stable but not
asymptotically stable.

11.87 Time-Varying Damping
For
m\ddot x+c(t)\dot x+kx=0
with
c(t)\ge0,
energy satisfies
\dot E=-c(t)\dot x^2\le0.

Proposition 11.29 — Lyapunov stability
under nonnegative time-varying damping

 The origin is Lyapunov stable.

Proof
The total mechanical energy is positive definite and
nonincreasing. ∎
Asymptotic convergence requires sufficient persistent
damping; c(t) could vanish too often to force decay.

11.88 Persistent Damping Condition
Suppose there exist T>0 and \alpha>0 such that
\int_t^{t+T}c(\tau)\,d\tau
\ge\alpha
for every t.
Under suitable oscillator observability conditions, this
persistent excitation of damping can imply asymptotic or
exponential decay.
The exact theorem depends on the time-varying system and
cannot be inferred from c(t)\ge0 alone.

11.89 Adaptive Damping Stability
Let
c(t)=c_0+\Delta c(t),

 with
c_0>0
and
\Delta c(t)\ge-c_0.
Then total damping remains nonnegative.
If adaptation is additionally bounded,
|\Delta c(t)|\le B_c,
the force remains bounded by
|F_d|
\le
(c_0+B_c)|v|.
This gives a simple robust passivity envelope.

11.90 Energy-Harvesting Controller
Audit
A complete audit should report:
1. mechanical equations;
2. transducer equations;
3. force and EMF constants;
4. electrical impedance;
5. converter efficiency;

 6. storage dynamics;
7. road-input model;
8. power-flow sign conventions;
9. suspension comfort metrics;
10.tire-load metrics;
11. actuator force, current, voltage, travel, and temperature
limits;
12.net energy after auxiliary consumption;
13.sensitivity to speed and road class;
14.failure-mode behavior;
15.independent validation.

11.91 Gross Versus Net Harvested
Energy
Define:
E_{\mathrm{gross}}
=
\int P_{\mathrm{generator,out}}dt.
Define total auxiliary and conversion cost:
E_{\mathrm{cost}}
=
E_{\mathrm{converter\,loss}}
+
E_{\mathrm{control}}
+
E_{\mathrm{sensing}}

 +
E_{\mathrm{storage\,loss}}.
Then
E_{\mathrm{net}}
=
E_{\mathrm{gross}}-E_{\mathrm{cost}}.
If an active suspension also consumes mechanical actuation
energy, that must be included separately.

11.92 Comparison with
Conventional Damping
A regenerative damper should be compared with a baseline
damper that would otherwise dissipate
E_{\mathrm{baseline}}
=
\int c_bv_r^2dt.
Define recovery fraction
\eta_{\mathrm{rec}}
=
\frac{
E_{\mathrm{net}}
}{
E_{\mathrm{baseline}}
}.

 This metric can exceed one only if the regenerative design
also changes the motion so that more mechanical energy
enters the suspension than in the baseline. It would not mean
conversion efficiency above 100%.

11.93 Equivalent Damping Match
To preserve comparable ride behavior, compare systems at
equal effective damping or equal comfort metrics.
Otherwise a harvester may appear to recover more energy
merely because it allows larger suspension motion or
imposes harsher damping.
Fair benchmarking requires matched operating constraints.

11.94 Control-Barrier Constraint
for Suspension Travel
Let suspension travel satisfy
|r|\le r_{\max}.
Define barrier function
h(r)=r_{\max}^2-r^2.
The safe set is
\mathcal S=\{r:h(r)\ge0\}.

 A control-barrier condition may require
\dot h+\alpha h\ge0.
Since
\dot h=-2r\dot r,
the condition is
-2r\dot r
+
\alpha(r_{\max}^2-r^2)
\ge0.
Higher-order barrier methods are required when the control
enters acceleration rather than velocity directly.

11.95 Tire-Contact Constraint
A simplified tire normal force is
F_t
=
F_{t0}
+
k_t(z_r-z_u)
under an appropriate reference convention.
Loss of contact occurs when
F_t\le0.

 A controller optimizing harvested power must preserve
F_t>0
with an appropriate safety margin.
Maximum energy recovery is unacceptable if it causes wheel
lift or severe tire-force variation.

11.96 Peak Force Constraint
For damper force
F_d=-c_ev_r,
a force limit gives
c_e
\le
\frac{F_{\max}}{|v_r|}
when v_r\neq0.
Thus the maximum allowable damping coefficient decreases
at high relative velocity.
A constant high damping command may saturate during
impacts.

11.97 Model Predictive Control
At each time step, solve

 \min_{u_0,\ldots,u_{N-1}}
\sum_{k=0}^{N-1}
\ell(x_k,u_k)
+
V_f(x_N)
subject to:
x_{k+1}=f(x_k,u_k,w_k),
u_kv_{r,k}\le0
for regenerative operation,
|u_k|\le F_{\max},
|r_k|\le r_{\max},
and storage constraints.
Only the first control input is applied, then the optimization
is repeated.

11.98 Recursive Feasibility
A model-predictive controller is recursively feasible if
feasibility at one step implies feasibility at the next under the
applied control and admissible disturbances.
This usually requires:
• a terminal invariant set;
• a backup control law;

 • disturbance margins.
Feasibility of one optimization instance alone does not
ensure future feasibility.

11.99 Stability of MPC
A common stability proof requires terminal cost V_f and
terminal controller \kappa_f satisfying
V_f(f(x,\kappa_f(x)))
V_f(x)
\le
-\ell(x,\kappa_f(x))
inside the terminal set.
Then the optimal finite-horizon value decreases along the
closed-loop trajectory and serves as a Lyapunov function.
Energy harvesting can be incorporated into \ell, but safety
and positive-definite regulation terms must remain sufficient
for stability.

11.100 Central Electromechanical
Conversion Theorem
Theorem 11.30 — Passive regenerative
transduction

 Consider a reciprocal linear transducer satisfying
F_{\mathrm{em}}=-k_ti,
e=k_tv,
and connected to a passive electrical network with stored
energy E_e and dissipation P_d\ge0.
Then the combined mechanical–electrical energy satisfies
\frac{d}{dt}
(E_m+E_e)
=
P_{\mathrm{external}}
P_d
P_{\mathrm{other\,mechanical\,loss}}.
Consequently, electrical energy delivered to a load cannot
exceed external mechanical input plus released initial stored
energy.

Proof
The electromechanical conversion terms are equal and
opposite in the mechanical and electrical energy balances
and therefore cancel internally. The remaining terms are
external power and nonnegative losses. Integrate over time. ∎

 11.101 Central Regenerative
Suspension Bound
Theorem 11.31 — Net recovery bound
Let a suspension system begin with stored energy E(0),
receive road and vehicle mechanical input
E_{\mathrm{in}},
deliver useful electrical output
E_{\mathrm{out}},
and incur total nonnegative losses E_{\mathrm{loss}}.
Then
E_{\mathrm{out}}
=
E_{\mathrm{in}}
+
E(0)
E(T)
E_{\mathrm{loss}},
and therefore
\boxed{
E_{\mathrm{out}}

 \le
E_{\mathrm{in}}+E(0)
}.

Proof
Integrate the total energy balance from 0 to T. Since
E(T)\ge0
and
E_{\mathrm{loss}}\ge0,
the inequality follows. ∎

11.102 Central Semi-Active Stability
Theorem
Theorem 11.32 — Stability under bounded
regenerative damping
Consider
m\ddot x+kx+c(t,x,\dot x)\dot x=0
with
m>0,
\qquad
k>0,

 \qquad
0<c_{\min}\le c(t,x,\dot x)\le c_{\max}.
Then the origin is globally asymptotically stable.

Proof
Use
V(x,\dot x)
=
\frac12m\dot x^2+\frac12kx^2.
Then
\dot V
=
-c(t,x,\dot x)\dot x^2
\le
-c_{\min}\dot x^2.
The derivative is nonpositive.
The set where
\dot V=0
is
\dot x=0.

In a magnetic circuit with saturation,

 13.56 No-Surplus Theorem
Theorem 13.17 — Resonant suspension
energy bound
For a periodic steady-state MAGPIE-type assembly with
high-frequency drive power P_d, mechanical disturbance
power P_m, useful electrical output P_o, and nonnegative
loss P_\ell,
\boxed{
\overline P_o
=
\overline P_d
+
\overline P_m
\overline P_\ell.
}
Consequently,
\boxed{
\overline P_o
\le
\overline P_d+\overline P_m.
}

Proof

 Integrate Poynting’s theorem and the mechanical energy
balance over the complete electromechanical system. In
periodic steady state, net stored-energy change over a full
number of cycles is zero. Internal electromechanical
conversion terms cancel, leaving external inputs, useful

14.1 The Original Insight
The original Howard Comma intuition was that ordinary
geometry can omit something structurally important.
Two objects may appear:
• far apart in ordinary space but function as one tightly
coupled unit;
• close together in ordinary space but interact weakly;
• geometrically aligned but operationally disconnected;

 • geometrically separated but connected through a
strong intermediary or shared pathway.
The first insight was therefore:
\text{visible distance}
\neq
\text{functional distance}.
The “comma” was conceived as the missing correction
between those two descriptions.
That insight was useful, but it was not yet mathematically
complete because the following remained unspecified:
1. What exactly counts as interaction?
2. How is interaction converted into distance?
3. When is that distance mathematically valid?
4. How are different units normalized?
5. How is the residual tested across triples or networks?
6. How is the model prevented from fitting its desired
conclusion circularly?
The perfected version answers each question explicitly.

14.2 Perfection Step One: Replace
Metaphor with Measurable Inputs
Let the entities be
x_1,\ldots,x_n.

 For every pair (i,j), define measurable quantities:
C_{ij}
for contact or direct coupling,
A_{ij}
for accessibility, transmissibility, or pathway strength,
and
d_{ij}
for ordinary geometric separation.
The interaction kernel is defined as
\boxed{
K_{ij}
=
w_C C_{ij}
+
w_A A_{ij}
+
w_D\phi(d_{ij})
}
with
w_C,w_A,w_D\ge0,
and

 w_C+w_A+w_D=1.
A standard geometric decay term is
\boxed{
\phi(d)=e^{-d/L},
}
where L>0 is an interaction-length scale.

This was the first major perfection: the Howard Comma
was no longer defined by an image or intuition alone. It
was grounded in declared pairwise measurements.

14.3 Why the Weight Constraints
Matter
The normalization
w_C+w_A+w_D=1
makes the kernel a convex combination of its
components.

Proposition 14.1 — Convex boundedness
Suppose
0\le C_{ij},A_{ij},\phi(d_{ij})\le1.

 Then
0\le K_{ij}\le1.

Proof
Because the weights are nonnegative and sum to one,
K_{ij} is a convex combination of three values in [0,1]. ∎
This provides a consistent numerical scale and prevents
arbitrary coefficient inflation from masquerading as
stronger interaction.

14.4 Perfection Step Two: Require
Symmetry
The kernel is required to satisfy
K_{ij}=K_{ji}.
This means the basic perfected formulation describes
reciprocal pairwise geometry.
If a system is direction dependent, one must either:
• symmetrize the directional measurements;
• construct separate forward and reverse kernels;
• or use a directed-geometry extension.

 The symmetric requirement was added because an
ordinary Euclidean kernel distance cannot generally be
derived from an arbitrary nonsymmetric matrix.

14.5 Perfection Step Three: Require
Positive Semidefiniteness
The decisive mathematical correction was the requirement
\boxed{
K\succeq0.
}
That means
a^TKa\ge0
for every vector a\in\mathbb R^n.
This is not merely a technical preference. It guarantees
that the interaction matrix can be interpreted as inner
products in a feature space.

Theorem 14.2 — Kernel embedding theorem
If K is symmetric and positive semidefinite, then there
exist feature vectors
\Psi(x_1),\ldots,\Psi(x_n)

\boxed{
K_{ij}
=
\left\langle
\Psi(x_i),\Psi(x_j)
\right\rangle.
}

Proof
Because K\succeq0, it has an eigendecomposition
K=Q\Lambda Q^T,
where
\Lambda=\operatorname{diag}(\lambda_1,\ldots,
\lambda_n),
\qquad
\lambda_a\ge0.
Define
\Phi=\Lambda^{1/2}Q^T.
Let \Psi(x_i) be the i-th column of \Phi. Then
\Phi^T\Phi
=
Q\Lambda Q^T

 =
K,
so
K_{ij}
=
\langle\Psi(x_i),\Psi(x_j)\rangle.
∎
This turned “functional relationship” into a genuine
geometry.

14.6 Perfection Step Four: Derive
Functional Distance from the
Kernel
The kernel-induced squared distance is

D_K(i,j)^2
=
K_{ii}+K_{jj}-2K_{ij}.

Using the feature-space representation,

+
\langle\Psi_j,\Psi_j\rangle
2\langle\Psi_i,\Psi_j\rangle\\
&=
\|\Psi_i-\Psi_j\|^2.

Therefore

D_K(i,j)
=
\|\Psi(x_i)-\Psi(x_j)\|.

The perfected formulation defines

D_K(i,j).

Usage

from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import heapq
import json
import math

from dataclasses import dataclass, field, asdict
from pathlib import Path
from typing import Any, Dict, List, Optional, Tuple

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Paths
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

DEFAULT_STATE_PATH = Path(__file__).resolve().parent / "scratchpad_state.json"

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Core law
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

def headroom(interior: float, claimed: float) -> float:
    return max(0.0, interior - claimed)


def overclaim(interior: float, claimed: float) -> float:
    return max(0.0, claimed - interior)


def solvent(interior: float, claimed: float, eps: float = 1e-12) -> bool:
    return claimed <= interior + eps

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Experience memory (priority heap: hardest residuals first)
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

@dataclass(order=True)
class Experience:
    priority: float
    signature: str = field(compare=False)
    residual: float = field(compare=False)
    action: str = field(compare=False)
    success: bool = field(compare=False)
    ts: float = field(compare=False, default_factory=time.time)
    note: str = field(compare=False, default="")

    def to_dict(self) -> Dict[str, Any]:
        return {
            "priority": self.priority,
            "signature": self.signature,
            "residual": self.residual,
            "action": self.action,
            "success": self.success,
            "ts": self.ts,
            "note": self.note,
        }

    @staticmethod
    def from_dict(d: Dict[str, Any]) -> "Experience":
        return Experience(
            priority=float(d["priority"]),
            signature=str(d["signature"]),
            residual=float(d["residual"]),
            action=str(d["action"]),
            success=bool(d["success"]),
            ts=float(d.get("ts", time.time())),
            note=str(d.get("note", "")),
        )

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Eyes — dual observation
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

@dataclass
class DualEyes:
    outward: float = 0.0   # observed residual in environment
    inward: float = 0.0    # self-audit residual on claims

    def agree(self, tol: float = 0.05) -> bool:
        return abs(self.outward - self.inward) <= tol and self.inward >= -1e-9

    def contract(self, amount: float = 0.02) -> None:
        self.outward = max(0.0, self.outward - amount)
        self.inward = max(0.0, self.inward - amount)

    def to_dict(self) -> Dict[str, float]:
        return {"outward": self.outward, "inward": self.inward}

    @staticmethod
    def from_dict(d: Dict[str, Any]) -> "DualEyes":
        return DualEyes(float(d.get("outward", 0.0)), float(d.get("inward", 0.0)))

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Gate
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

@dataclass
class SolvencyGate:
    cool_off: int = 0

    def admit(self, interior: float, claimed: float, cost: float) -> bool:
        if self.cool_off > 0:
            return False
        return cost <= headroom(interior, claimed) + 1e-12

    def tick(self) -> None:
        if self.cool_off > 0:
            self.cool_off -= 1

    def refuse(self, severity: int = 3) -> None:
        self.cool_off = max(self.cool_off, severity)

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Policy — raised starting line weights
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

@dataclass
class Policy:
    """Action weights; higher = preferred when solvent."""
    observe: float = 0.35
    amortize: float = 0.30
    advance: float = 0.20
    hold: float = 0.15

    def normalized(self) -> Dict[str, float]:
        m = {
            "observe": max(1e-6, self.observe),
            "amortize": max(1e-6, self.amortize),
            "advance": max(1e-6, self.advance),
            "hold": max(1e-6, self.hold),
        }
        s = sum(m.values())
        return {k: v / s for k, v in m.items()}

    def pick(self, rng: random.Random) -> str:
        n = self.normalized()
        keys, weights = zip(*n.items())
        return rng.choices(list(keys), weights=list(weights), k=1)[0]

    def reinforce(self, action: str, success: bool, lr: float = 0.04) -> None:
        attr = action if action in ("observe", "amortize", "advance", "hold") else "hold"
        cur = getattr(self, attr)
        if success:
            setattr(self, attr, cur + lr)
        else:
            setattr(self, attr, max(0.05, cur - lr * 1.5))

    def to_dict(self) -> Dict[str, float]:
        return asdict(self)

    @staticmethod
    def from_dict(d: Dict[str, Any]) -> "Policy":
        return Policy(
            observe=float(d.get("observe", 0.35)),
            amortize=float(d.get("amortize", 0.30)),
            advance=float(d.get("advance", 0.20)),
            hold=float(d.get("hold", 0.15)),
        )

        # Solvency state
        self.interior: float = 0.18
        self.claimed: float = 0.0
        self.skill: float = 0.35
        self.starting_line: float = 0.0
        self.generation: int = 1
        self.field_residual: float = 0.25

        self.eyes = DualEyes()
        self.gate = SolvencyGate()
        self.policy = Policy()
        self.memory: List[Experience] = []  # heap by priority
        self.step_count: int = 0
        self.success_streak: int = 0
        self.total_insolvencencies: int = 0

        if self.state_path.exists():
            self.load()

        # Apply raised starting line to interior floor
        self.interior = max(self.interior, 0.18 + self.starting_line * 0.05)

    # ----- persistence -----

    def to_dict(self) -> Dict[str, Any]:
        return {
            "interior": self.interior,
            "claimed": self.claimed,
            "skill": self.skill,
            "starting_line": self.starting_line,
            "generation": self.generation,
            "field_residual": self.field_residual,
            "eyes": self.eyes.to_dict(),
            "cool_off": self.gate.cool_off,
            "policy": self.policy.to_dict(),
            "memory": [e.to_dict() for e in sorted(self.memory)[:200]],
            "step_count": self.step_count,
            "success_streak": self.success_streak,
            "total_insolvencencies": self.total_insolvencencies,
        }

    def load(self) -> None:
        try:
            data = json.loads(self.state_path.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
        except Exception:
            return
        self.interior = float(data.get("interior", self.interior))
        self.claimed = float(data.get("claimed", 0.0))
        self.skill = float(data.get("skill", self.skill))
        self.starting_line = float(data.get("starting_line", 0.0))
        self.generation = int(data.get("generation", 1))
        self.field_residual = float(data.get("field_residual", 0.25))
        self.eyes = DualEyes.from_dict(data.get("eyes", {}))
        self.gate.cool_off = int(data.get("cool_off", 0))
        self.policy = Policy.from_dict(data.get("policy", {}))
        self.memory = [Experience.from_dict(x) for x in data.get("memory", [])]
        heapq.heapify(self.memory)
        self.step_count = int(data.get("step_count", 0))
        self.success_streak = int(data.get("success_streak", 0))
        self.total_insolvencencies = int(data.get("total_insolvencencies", 0))

    def save(self) -> None:
        self.state_path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
        self.state_path.write_text(
            json.dumps(self.to_dict(), indent=2, sort_keys=True),
            encoding="utf-8",
        )

    # ----- metrics -----

    @property
    def R_plus(self) -> float:
        return headroom(self.interior, self.claimed)

    @property
    def R_minus(self) -> float:
        return overclaim(self.interior, self.claimed)

    def status(self) -> str:
        n = self.policy.normalized()
        return (
            f"gen={self.generation} line={self.starting_line:.3f} skill={self.skill:.3f}\n"
            f"interior={self.interior:.3f} claimed={self.claimed:.3f} "
            f"R+={self.R_plus:.3f} R-={self.R_minus:.3f}\n"
            f"field={self.field_residual:.3f} cool_off={self.gate.cool_off} "
            f"streak={self.success_streak} eyes={'AGREE' if self.eyes.agree() else 'SPLIT'}\n"
            f"policy={{{', '.join(f'{k}:{v:.2f}' for k,v in n.items())}}}"
        )

    # ----- memory -----

    def remember(
        self,
        signature: str,
        residual: float,
        action: str,
        success: bool,
        note: str = "",
    ) -> None:
        # Higher residual failures get more priority (lower heap value via negation)
        priority = -residual if not success else -residual * 0.3
        exp = Experience(
            priority=priority,
            signature=signature,
            residual=residual,
            action=action,
            success=success,
            note=note,
        )
        heapq.heappush(self.memory, exp)
        if len(self.memory) > 300:
            self.memory = list(heapq.nsmallest(200, self.memory))
            heapq.heapify(self.memory)

    def hardest(self, k: int = 5) -> List[Experience]:
        return list(heapq.nsmallest(k, self.memory))

    # ----- actions -----

    def act_observe(self) -> Tuple[bool, str]:
        cost = 0.012
        if not self.gate.admit(self.interior, self.claimed, cost):
            self.gate.refuse(2)
            self.remember("observe_refused", self.field_residual, "observe", False, "gate")
            return False, "GATE REFUSED observe"
        self.claimed += cost
        self.field_residual = max(0.02, self.field_residual - 0.03 * (1.0 + self.skill))
        self.eyes.contract(0.02)
        self.eyes.outward = self.field_residual * 0.8
        self.skill = min(0.95, self.skill + 0.004)
        self.remember("observe", self.field_residual, "observe", True)
        return True, "OBSERVED residual contracted"

    def act_amortize(self) -> Tuple[bool, str]:
        if self.claimed <= 1e-6:
            return True, "NOTHING TO AMORTIZE"
        before = self.claimed
        # skill improves amortization efficiency
        factor = 0.65 - 0.15 * self.skill
        self.claimed *= max(0.35, factor)
        self.field_residual = max(0.02, self.field_residual - 0.015)
        self.eyes.inward = max(0.0, self.eyes.inward - 0.02)
        self.remember("amortize", before - self.claimed, "amortize", True)
        return True, f"AMORTIZED claimed {before:.3f}->{self.claimed:.3f}"

    def act_advance(self) -> Tuple[bool, str]:
        """Push into field; costs headroom; risks insolvency if field high."""
        cost = 0.03 + 0.02 * self.field_residual
        if not self.gate.admit(self.interior, self.claimed, cost):
            self.gate.refuse(4)
            self.total_insolvencencies += 1
            self.success_streak = 0
            self.remember("advance_refused", cost, "advance", False, "insufficient headroom")
            self.policy.reinforce("advance", False)
            return False, "GATE REFUSED advance"
        self.claimed += cost
        # success more likely if field residual low and skill high
        difficulty = self.field_residual * (1.0 - 0.5 * self.skill)
        success = self.rng.random() > difficulty * 0.9
        if success:
            self.success_streak += 1
            self.interior = min(0.45, self.interior + 0.004)
            self.field_residual = max(0.02, self.field_residual - 0.01)
            self.policy.reinforce("advance", True)
            self.remember("advance", difficulty, "advance", True)
            return True, "ADVANCE ok"
        else:
            self.success_streak = 0
            self.field_residual = min(1.0, self.field_residual + 0.04)
            self.eyes.outward = self.field_residual
            self.policy.reinforce("advance", False)
            self.remember("advance_fail", difficulty, "advance", False, "field pushback")
            return False, "ADVANCE failed — field pushback"

    def act_hold(self) -> Tuple[bool, str]:
        self.claimed = max(0.0, self.claimed * 0.97)
        self.gate.tick()
        self.remember("hold", self.R_minus, "hold", True)
        return True, "HOLD settle"

    # ----- obstacles (demo / live residual field) -----

    def emit_obstacle(self) -> Dict[str, Any]:
        mag = 0.02 + self.rng.random() * 0.08 + self.starting_line * 0.01
        channels = ["factual", "logical", "social", "tool"]
        obs = {
            "mag": mag,
            "channel": self.rng.choice(channels),
            "signature": f"obs_{self.step_count}_{self.rng.randint(0,9999)}",
        }
        self.field_residual = min(1.0, self.field_residual + mag * 0.35)
        self.eyes.outward = self.field_residual
        return obs

    def absorb_obstacle(self, obs: Dict[str, Any]) -> Tuple[bool, str]:
        mag = float(obs["mag"])
        if mag <= self.R_plus + 1e-12:
            self.claimed += mag
            self.success_streak += 1
            self.field_residual = max(0.02, self.field_residual - 0.02)
            self.remember(obs["signature"], mag, "absorb", True, obs["channel"])
            return True, f"ABSORBED {obs['channel']} mag={mag:.3f}"
        self.gate.refuse(5)
        self.total_insolvencencies += 1
        self.success_streak = 0
        self.remember(obs["signature"], mag, "absorb", False, "insolvency")
        return False, f"INSOLVENCY {obs['channel']} mag={mag:.3f}"

    # ----- generation / starting line -----

    def raise_starting_line(self, amount: float = 0.04) -> None:
        self.starting_line = min(1.0, self.starting_line + amount + 0.01 * self.skill)
        self.generation += 1
        # inherit: policy kept, memory kept, interior floor rises
        self.interior = max(self.interior, 0.18 + self.starting_line * 0.05)
        self.claimed = 0.0
        self.gate.cool_off = 0

    def new_generation_after_failure(self) -> None:
        self.raise_starting_line(0.04)
        # slight policy humility
        self.policy.reinforce("advance", False)
        self.policy.reinforce("observe", True)

    # ----- main improve cycle -----

    def choose_action(self) -> str:
        # If insolvent or cool-off: force amortize/hold/observe
        if self.gate.cool_off > 0 or self.R_minus > 0:
            return self.rng.choice(["amortize", "hold", "observe"])
        if self.field_residual > 0.55:
            return self.rng.choice(["observe", "amortize", "observe"])
        if self.claimed > 0.6 * self.interior:
            return "amortize"
        return self.policy.pick(self.rng)

    def step(self) -> str:
        self.step_count += 1
        self.gate.tick()
        action = self.choose_action()
        if action == "observe":
            ok, msg = self.act_observe()
        elif action == "amortize":
            ok, msg = self.act_amortize()
        elif action == "advance":
            ok, msg = self.act_advance()
        else:
            ok, msg = self.act_hold()
        self.policy.reinforce(action, ok)
        # self-audit eye tracks claim pressure
        self.eyes.inward = min(1.0, self.R_minus + self.claimed * 0.5)
        return f"step={self.step_count} action={action} ok={ok} | {msg}"

    def improve(self, cycles: int = 25, obstacles: bool = True) -> List[str]:
        log: List[str] = []
        for i in range(cycles):
            if obstacles and self.rng.random() < 0.25:
                obs = self.emit_obstacle()
                ok, msg = self.absorb_obstacle(obs)
                log.append(msg)
                if not ok:
                    self.new_generation_after_failure()
                    log.append(
                        f"RAISED LINE -> {self.starting_line:.3f} gen={self.generation}"
                    )
            line = self.step()
            log.append(line)
            # learn from hardest experiences periodically
            if i % 7 == 0 and self.memory:
                hard = self.hardest(3)
                for e in hard:
                    if not e.success and e.action == "advance":
                        self.policy.reinforce("observe", True)
        self.save()
        return log

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# CLI
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

def main() -> None:
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description="Residual-aware scratchpad")
    parser.add_argument("--demo", action="store_true", help="run demo improvement cycles")
    parser.add_argument("--status", action="store_true", help="print status only")
    parser.add_argument("--reset", action="store_true", help="raise line / new gen, clear claimed")
    parser.add_argument("--cycles", type=int, default=25, help="improvement cycles")
    parser.add_argument(
        "--state",
        type=str,
        default=str(DEFAULT_STATE_PATH),
        help="path to JSON state",
    )
    args = parser.parse_args()

    sp = Scratchpad(state_path=Path(args.state))

    if args.status:
        print(sp.status())
        return

    if args.reset:
        sp.raise_starting_line(0.02)
        sp.save()
        print("reset generation")
        print(sp.status())
        return

    cycles = args.cycles if args.demo or args.cycles else 25
    print("=== scratchpad improve ===")
    print(sp.status())
    print("----")
    log = sp.improve(cycles=cycles, obstacles=True)
    for line in log[-15:]:
        print(line)
    print("----")
    print(sp.status())
    print(f"saved: {sp.state_path}")

if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()
